newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge says may have to de-consolidate BBL.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge says may have to de-consolidate BBL.

text.p: Belgian insurer Royale Belge said on Wednesday it might be forced to deconsolidate its stake in Belgian bank Banque Bruxelles Lambert if the European Commission vetoed a BBL shareholder pact.
"That is a potential danger," Royale Belge managing director Jean-Pierre Gerard told a news briefing.

The Commission is considering legal action to force changes to the pact between holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL), Royale Belge and bank Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet, which together own 37.5 percent of BBL.
The Commission warned the year-old agreement could breach EU anti-trust law.

Royale Belge, which said earlier on Wednesday first-half 1996 group net profit rose 13.7 percent to 5.07 billion francs, consolidated for the first time in half-year earnings its 12.5 percent stake in BBL.
Gerard did not expect the Commission to take a decision soon -- not before the end of the 1996 accounts.
But Gerard said Royale Belge would hold on to its BBL stake whatever the Commission's decision.
"The decision of the Commission will not change our position," he said.
